justification: The package contains a very large, monolithic class JavaSymbolSolver that centralizes many responsibilities: injection, resolution for many different AST node types (MethodDeclaration, ClassOrInterfaceDeclaration, EnumDeclaration, RecordDeclaration, EnumConstantDeclaration, ConstructorDeclaration, AnnotationDeclaration, AnnotationMemberDeclaration, FieldDeclaration, VariableDeclarator, MethodCallExpr, ObjectCreationExpr, NameExpr, MethodReferenceExpr, FieldAccessExpr, ThisExpr, ExplicitConstructorInvocationStmt, Parameter, AnnotationExpr, TypePatternExpr), multiple parameter-resolution helpers, type conversion and calculation, and a nested ArrayLengthValueDeclaration. The class has numerous long methods with many conditional branches handling many distinct cases (i.e., high LOC and high complexity). The package also includes another substantial class, SourceFileInfoExtractor, which adds file traversal, parsing and reporting responsibilities. The concentration of many behaviors and large code size (including duplicated/very long definitions in the provided input) indicates the component is excessively large and centralizes too many concerns, which matches the God Component smell.

The concentration of so many classes and responsibilities in this single package/module (and large source size with duplicated/extended blocks) increases cognitive load, coupling, and violates the single-responsibility separation expected for smaller components — matching the God Component smell.
